title: Restriction sequence and cohomology for a fixed injective hyperplane section
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\geq1$, $X=\mathbf P^n_k$ with twists [def-pc-projective-space-twist], and $E$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$ be nonzero and let $i:H=V(s)\hookrightarrow X$ be the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of its zero scheme $V(s)=Z(s)$ [def-pc-zero-scheme]. Put $G=i^*E$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and $G(d)=G\otimes i^*\mathcal O_X(d)$. Assume $G$ is coherent and multiplication by $s$ on $E(d-1)\to E(d)$ is injective for every integer $d$. For each $d\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical restriction map gives a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow E(d-1)\xrightarrow{s}E(d)\longrightarrow i_*G(d)\longrightarrow0,$$
where $(i_*M)(U)=M(i^{-1}U)$ with the induced $\mathcal O_X(U)$-action. The natural edge map identifies $H^q(X,i_*G(d))$ with $H^q(H,G(d))$ for every $q\geq0$, using module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] and the edge map of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. Thus the associated long exact sequence begins
$$0\longrightarrow H^0(X,E(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^0(X,E(d))\xrightarrow{r_d}H^0(H,G(d))\longrightarrow H^1(X,E(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^1(X,E(d))\longrightarrow\cdots,$$
and has consecutive terms
$$H^q(X,E(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^q(X,E(d))\longrightarrow H^q(H,G(d))\longrightarrow H^{q+1}(X,E(d-1)).$$
The maps to cohomology on $H$ are the canonical restriction maps. Restriction $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))\to H^0(H,i^*\mathcal O_X(1))$ is surjective. For $u\in H^0(X,E(d))$ and $v\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$, one has
$$r_{d+1}(uv)=r_d(u)\,(v|_H),$$
where products use the canonical twist multiplications, locally $e_j^{(d)}\otimes e_j^{(1)}\mapsto e_j^{(d+1)}$.

source.place: Tag 089Z (lemma-hyperplane, including its coordinate proof), Tag 08A0 (lemma-exact-sequence-induction, local description of the quotient after injectivity is given), and Tag 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology). Fixed-section variant: the infinite-field hypothesis of 08A0 is needed only to choose an injective section; here injectivity is a hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix $d\in\mathbf Z$ and write $J=\mathcal I_H$. On any open trivializing $\mathcal O_X(1)$, write $s=ae$; the zero-scheme definition gives $J=(a)$. The twist multiplication identifies the map $E(d-1)\to E(d)$ with multiplication by $a$ in these frames, so its image is exactly $J E(d)$. The closed-immersion unit-quotient theorem, applied to the module $E(d)$, says that $\eta_d:E(d)\to i_*i^*E(d)$ is onto and has kernel $J E(d)$. The canonical pullback-tensor isomorphism identifies $i^*E(d)=i^*(E\otimes\mathcal O_X(d))$ with $G\otimes i^*\mathcal O_X(d)=G(d)$. Compose $\eta_d$ with this identification to obtain the canonical restriction $\rho_d:E(d)\to i_*G(d)$. Its kernel is the image of multiplication by $s$, and that multiplication is injective by hypothesis. This proves the asserted short exact sequence. The quotient calculation itself used no coherence hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 08A0 (lemma-exact-sequence-induction, local quotient calculation) and 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology), adapted to a prescribed section whose multiplication is injective.

proof.text: Check the hypotheses needed for the cohomology edge map. The standard opens of $X$ are $U_j=\operatorname{Spec} A_j$ with $A_j=k[T_l/T_j:l\ne j]$: in the degree-zero localization describing $D_+(T_j)$, a degree-zero monomial is a product of these ratios, which are algebraically independent. The local zero-scheme formula gives $H\cap U_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j/(a_j))$, where $a_j$ represents $s$ in the frame $T_j$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$); the finite-type-algebra Noetherian theorem therefore makes each $A_j/(a_j)$ Noetherian. These affine opens cover $H$, so $H$ is locally Noetherian. By the coherent/quasi-coherent finite-type equivalence, the assumed coherent $G$ is quasi-coherent. Each $i^*\mathcal O_X(d)$ is locally free of rank one: pulling back its displayed local frame gives a frame, directly from the tensor definition of pullback. Hence $G(d)$ is locally isomorphic to $G$, so is quasi-coherent as well. Finally $i$ is affine, by the affine-quotient characterization of a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 089Z (lemma-hyperplane), local equations; coherent.tex Tag 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian); Noetherianity is checked on the displayed affine charts.

proof.text:
The category of module sheaves on $X$ is abelian with enough injectives, and $\Gamma(X,-)$ is additive and left exact, by the two cited module-category theorems. Apply the derived-functor long-exact-sequence theorem to the short exact sequence of Step 1. Since module cohomology is right derived global sections, it gives
$$0\to H^0(X,E(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^0(X,E(d))\xrightarrow{H^0(\rho_d)}H^0(X,i_*G(d))\to H^1(X,E(d-1))\to\cdots$$
and, for every $q\ge0$, the terms $H^q(X,E(d-1))\xrightarrow{s}H^q(X,E(d))\to H^q(X,i_*G(d))\to H^{q+1}(X,E(d-1))$.

By Step 2, the affine-morphism cohomology-edge theorem applies to $i$ and $G(d)$: the specified edge map $e_{i,G(d)}:H^q(X,i_*G(d))\to H^q(H,G(d))$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$. Replace the corresponding terms of the sequence in Step 3 using this isomorphism, and define the new boundary by composing the old boundary with $e_{i,G(d)}^{-1}$; composition with isomorphisms preserves equality of kernels and images. This gives exactly both displayed cohomology sequences in the statement. To identify the arrows, the composition clause for cohomology of module maps gives
$$e_{i,G(d)}\circ H^q(\rho_d)=(\rho_d)^*.$$
Here $\rho_d$ is the $i$-map obtained from the pullback unit followed by $i^*E(d)\cong G(d)$ in Step 1; by the definition of module-cohomology pullback this is the canonical restriction map. In degree zero the degree-zero clause identifies it with the actual map on global sections. Thus the identifications use the specified edge map, including the restriction arrows, rather than just abstract isomorphisms of groups.

The projective-twist cohomology calculation identifies $s$ with a linear form $\sum_{l=0}^n b_lT_l$ having at least one nonzero coefficient. On $U_j$, its multiplier is the nonzero polynomial $a_j=b_j+\sum_{l\ne j}b_l(T_l/T_j)$. Multiplication by $a_j$ is injective on $A_j$: for any nonzero polynomial $f$, the leading coefficient of $a_jf$ in a monomial order is the product of two nonzero coefficients in the field $k$, so $a_jf\ne0$. This remains injective after localization (if $a_j f/t=0$, some allowed denominator $u$ has $u a_j f=0$, hence $u f=0$). Thus $s:\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_X(1)$ is injective. Apply the quotient-and-pullback-tensor calculation of Step 1 with $E=\mathcal O_X$ and $d=1$ to get
$$0\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{s}\mathcal O_X(1)\to i_*i^*\mathcal O_X(1)\to0.$$
The long exact sequence from Step 3 and the equality of degree-zero direct-image sections give
$$H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))\to H^0(H,i^*\mathcal O_X(1))\to H^1(X,\mathcal O_X).$$
The same projective-twist cohomology theorem gives $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)=0$ for every $n\ge1$, including $n=1$. Exactness therefore proves the asserted surjectivity over every field.

proof.text: For $u\in H^0(X,E(d))$ and $v\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$, the pullback-tensor isomorphism sends $i^*(u\otimes v)$ to $i^*u\otimes i^*v$. On each standard trivializing open, the twist product sends $m e_j^{(d)}\otimes c e_j^{(1)}$ to $(cm)e_j^{(d+1)}$. After restriction both coefficients are mapped to $\mathcal O_H$, and the resulting product is $\bar c\bar m$ in either order of operations. These local equalities agree on overlaps since they use the canonical twist multiplications. Since Step 4 identified $r_d$ with this restriction on sections, they give $r_{d+1}(uv)=r_d(u)(v|_H)$.
